results.name: Joby Aviation (JOBY) Stock Declines Pre-Market Following $500M Resonant Sciences Acquisition Announcement - Blockonomi
results.content:
## Key Highlights  
- Joby Aviation announces $500 million acquisition of Resonant Sciences to bolster defense capabilities.
- Acquisition brings more than $100 million in annual revenue to Joby’s defense operations.
- Shares decline 4.98% in premarket activity to $8.39 following previous session’s 1.97% gain to $8.81.
- Transaction includes secure facilities, radio frequency technology, and existing defense contracts.
- Deal anticipated to finalize during first half of 2027 pending regulatory clearance.  
Shares of Joby Aviation experienced early morning selling pressure following the company’s disclosure of a significant defense sector acquisition. Pre-market trading showed JOBY at $8.39, representing a 4.98% decline from the prior session’s closing price of $8.81, which had finished 1.97% higher. The aerospace firm revealed plans to purchase Resonant Sciences in a transaction valued at roughly $500 million.
## Strategic Defense Expansion Through Resonant Sciences Buyout  
This strategic acquisition positions Joby Aviation to significantly strengthen its defense technology portfolio with an operational business serving national security interests. Resonant Sciences maintains a financially healthy defense operation supporting ongoing United States security initiatives. The deal provides [Joby](https://coincentral.com/joby-aviation-joby-stock-pops-3-after-crushing-revenue-estimates/) with instant access to secure infrastructure, manufacturing operations, specialized personnel, and established governmental connections.  
Following regulatory clearance, Resonant Sciences will function as Joby’s specialized defense division. The acquired entity will maintain its current branding with J. Micah North continuing as chief executive. Joby plans to consolidate its current defense initiatives under this expanded operational unit.  
Current defense programs encompass turbine-electric aircraft development, hydrogen-powered electric platforms, and autonomous systems engineered for military and civilian applications. Joby’s commercial aviation segment will maintain its focus on electric air taxi regulatory approval and manufacturing operations. This organizational approach creates separation between defense technology development and Joby’s primary commercial aviation efforts while growing both divisions.
## Financial Performance and Technology Portfolio of Resonant Sciences  
Resonant Sciences maintains a workforce of approximately 250 employees specializing in sophisticated radio frequency technologies for defense applications. The organization manufactures sensor systems, communication platforms, electronic warfare capabilities, and autonomous solutions. Its product lineup serves government entities and prominent defense industry contractors participating in multiple ongoing programs.  
Annual revenue grew approximately 40% year-over-year, surpassing $100 million over the trailing twelve-month period. The company achieved adjusted EBITDA margins in the high-teens range during recent reporting periods. Leadership anticipates improved profitability as manufacturing volumes scale across recently secured defense contracts.  
Order intake during the initial half of 2026 tripled compared to the prior year period. Simultaneously, Resonant’s contract backlog expanded to more than double the previous year’s levels. These metrics provide [Joby](https://coincentral.com/joby-aviation-joby-stock-rises-4-after-toyota-manufacturing-deal/) with an established revenue foundation as it accelerates its defense technology initiatives.

results.name: Joby expands defense business with $500 million acquisition of Resonant Sciences - Air Data News
results.content:
**Joby Aviation** has agreed to acquire defense technology company **Resonant Sciences** for approximately $500 million, giving the company a much larger presence in the military sector while keeping its commercial electric air taxi business separate.  
Under the agreement, expected to close in the first half of 2027, Resonant will become Joby's dedicated defense business and will continue to operate under its own name and management. Joby said its commercial division will continue to pursue certification and entry into service of its electric air taxi.  
**Follow Air Data News:** **WhatsApp** | **Instagram** | **LinkedIn** | **Twitter** | **Facebook**  
Founded in 2015 and based in Dayton, Ohio, Resonant Sciences develops radio-frequency (RF) systems, mission equipment, electronic warfare technologies and low-observable aircraft structures for U.S. government agencies and major defense contractors. The company employs about 250 people and generated more than $100 million in revenue over the past 12 months.  
[Joby](https://www.airdatanews.com/joby-flies-first-certification-aircraft-as-air-taxi-program-moves-toward-approval/) plans to combine its turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft programs, autonomy software and propulsion technologies with Resonant's expertise in sensing, communications and mission systems. The company said the combination will open opportunities in autonomous military aircraft and other defense applications.
The acquisition also gives Joby an established defense business with classified facilities, long-term government contracts and manufacturing operations. Resonant currently operates more than 100,000 square feet of engineering and production space, and another 125,000-square-foot facility is under construction. Together with Joby's existing sites in Ohio, the combined operation will total nearly one million square feet dedicated to aerospace and defense activities.  
The announcement came one day after [Archer Aviation](https://www.airdatanews.com/former-rivals-unite-as-archer-acquires-three-boeing-aerospace-subsidiaries/) revealed its own move into the defense sector through the acquisition of three Boeing subsidiaries: autonomous aircraft developer Wisk Aero, drone manufacturer Insitu and digital aviation company SkyGrid.
##### Related news  
[Allegiant to acquire Sun Country in $1.5bn cash and stock deal](https://www.airdatanews.com/allegiant-acquires-sun-country-1-5bn/)  
January 12, 2026  
The two transactions point to a similar strategy among leading urban air mobility developers. Both Joby and Archer continue to pursue FAA certification of their electric aircraft, but military customers offer another source of revenue in autonomy, unmanned aircraft and advanced mission systems.  
Defense procurement also follows a different path from commercial passenger certification, which may allow the two companies to generate business sooner while their civil aircraft complete the regulatory process.

results.name: Joby to buy Resonant Sciences, establish defense business in $500 million deal - Breaking Defense
results.content:
WASHINGTON — Electric aircraft startup [Joby Aviation](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/joby/) has agreed to acquire the military technology firm Resonant Sciences and convert the Dayton, Ohio-based company into Joby’s dedicated defense business, the two companies announced today.  
The $500 million acquisition consists of roughly $450 million in cash and $50 million in Joby common stock, according to a joint [press release](https://www.jobyaviation.com/news/joby-aviation-to-scale-defense-business-through-acquisition-of-resonant-sciences) from both companies. The transaction is expected to close “in the first half of 2027,” subject to regulatory approval.  
Joby is one of several electric air taxi services racing to market targeting point-to-point shuttling in urban environments — an ambition broadly slowed by developmental challenges and regulatory hurdles. The company was one of several vendors that previously pitched all-electric air vehicles to military users, but testing with the US Air Force found that fully electrified aircraft [lacked the range necessary](https://aviationweek.com/defense/aircraft-propulsion/afwerx-says-agility-prime-evtols-lack-range-shifts-hybrid) for more demanding defense missions.
However, Joby hasn’t given up on Pentagon contracts. The company said its acquisition of Resonant — which manufactures radio frequency (RF) and mission systems, among other technologies — aims to exploit “a broader shift in defense priorities toward” low-cost autonomous aircraft that feature resilient communications, sensing and electronic countermeasures.  
After the transaction closes, Resonant will continue operating under its current name as Joby’s defense unit led by Resonant co-founder and CEO J. Micah North, the press release says. Joby plans to combine its existing military work under its new defense arm, with a focus on developing autonomous tech and “dual-use turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft.” Joby’s commercial efforts would then similarly be concentrated on the civil market for its [all-electric S4 air taxi](https://www.jobyaviation.com/technology).  
“Resonant has built an exceptional business that combines advanced technology, vertically integrated production capabilities and deep customer trust,” Joby founder and CEO JoeBen Bevirt said in the release. “The combination will pair Resonant’s established capabilities with Joby’s globally leading aircraft propulsion technologies, creating a powerful platform for the next phase of Resonant’s growth.”
“Resonant Sciences’ experienced, defense-focused team and established cleared infrastructure will eliminate this constraint,” the spokesperson said. “Following the acquisition, Joby will have the cleared personnel and FCL \[facility clearance] necessary to participate more directly in classified engagements, assume a greater share of classified engineering and program responsibilities, and engage with government customers at a level that was previously difficult to support independently.”  
The spokesperson added that the new defense unit established by absorbing Resonant’s staff “should enhance the value of the L3Harris partnership rather than duplicate or displace L3Harris’ role” and position Joby as a “stronger long-term partner for L3Harris and Joby’s other defense partners.”  
News of Joby’s acquisition of Resonant marks a second shake up in the air taxi industry this week. On Monday, Archer Aviation [announced](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/08/boeing-to-sell-three-subsidiaries-to-evtol-firm-archer/) it would buy three Boeing subsidiaries, which among other provisions would see Boeing take a sizable stake in Archer.
